# Is SafeFall a general safety layer that needs no controller-specific retraining and guarantees damage-free falls on arbitrary terrain?

> **Current answer:** SafeFall uses a GRU to predict imminent failure of a nominal policy and hands control to a protective policy. The paper reduces contact force and joint torque in simulation and reports a limited hardware impulse experiment. The predictor must be retrained when the nominal policy changes, the environments are flat or nearly flat, and no public implementation was found, so this is not a cross-platform, all-terrain safety guarantee.

- **Handbook level:** `L3 Reviewed engineering conclusion`

- SafeFall uses a GRU to predict imminent failure of a nominal policy and hands control to a protective policy. The paper reduces contact force and joint torque in simulation and reports a limited hardware impulse experiment. The predictor must be retrained when the nominal policy changes, the environments are flat or nearly flat, and no public implementation was found, so this is not a cross-platform, all-terrain safety guarantee.
